Coffee Cup Sustainability, An Observational Study

What am I observing?

Between March and May 2026, I observed coffee cup usage across three types of locations in Auckland:

University campus (student cafes)

Chain cafes (Starbucks, etc.)

Local cafes (independent coffee shops)

For each observation, I recorded:

Whether the cup was reusable or disposable

The person’s estimated age group

The hour of day

The location

Total observations: 60 coffee consumers

Does age affect coffee cup choice?

The bar chart above reveals a clear pattern. People under 20 and in their 20s are more likely to use disposable cups. In contrast, the 30s, 40s, and 50s age groups show much higher proportions of reusable cups.

This makes sense practically: younger people may be students with less disposable income to invest in a reusable cup, or they might be more likely to buy coffee on impulse. Older consumers might plan their coffee purchases more deliberately.

What’s interesting is that the 50s age group had the highest count of reusable cups observed.

When do people use reusable cups?

The time of day tells an interesting story. At 8am (early morning rush), disposable cups dominate - only about 20% of coffee drinkers used reusable cups. This likely reflects people rushing to work or class, grabbing whatever is fastest.

Reusable cup usage peaks around 11am and 2pm (reaching nearly 50%), when people might be taking a proper break, sitting down in the cafe, and deliberately choosing to use their reusable cup.

By late afternoon (3pm-4pm), disposable cups increase again, possibly as people grab an afternoon pick-me-up on the go.

Are people switching to reusable cups over time?

This is the most encouraging finding. Looking at observations from late March to early May 2026, there is a clear upward trend in reusable cup usage.

In late March, approximately 30% of observed coffee drinkers used reusable cups. By early May, this had increased to over 50% - meaning reusable cups were actually more common than disposable ones in my final observations.

The three locations (university campus, chain cafes, local cafes) all showed similar upward movement, though local cafes consistently had slightly higher reusable rates.

What does this mean?

My observational study suggests that:

Age matters - sustainability campaigns might need to target younger consumers

Time matters - morning rush = more disposable, mid-day = more reusable

Time also matters across dates - reusable cup adoption appears to be increasing

The upward trend is particularly hopeful. Whether this reflects growing environmental awareness, new sustainability policies, or simply warmer weather encouraging people to carry reusable bottles, it suggests positive change is happening.
